title: Rad1-Rad10 uses different interfaces to interact with pathway-specific DNA repair factors.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed both deposited coordinate files: 10QY (Rad1-Rad10-Saw1, cryo-EM, 3 protein chains, 8,561 ATOM records, 3.7 Angstrom resolution, 1.0 MB mmCIF) and 10QX (Rad1-Rad10, 2 chains, 6,512 atoms, 4.5 Angstrom, 0.8 MB). Confirmed the RCSB entry metadata links both to this paper's DOI. Listed the Europe PMC supplement: 15 files, all of them figure images plus one 11.8 MB supplementary PDF; no tabular data file of any kind.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The data availability statement, read in the open-access full text: 'All other data and reagents in this article will be shared upon request to the corresponding author.' The existence and content of supplementary tables S1 (plasmids/strains/primers) and the cryo-EM statistics table are known from in-text citations only; I did not open the 11.8 MB supplementary PDF because the file listing shows it is a PDF of figures and tables, not a machine-readable data table.

a1_downloadable.note: Split outcome, and the half that matters fails. The two cryo-EM structures download freely and I opened both. But every quantitative experimental result in the paper (yeast UV-survival and double-strand-break repair assays, binding/pull-down experiments, nuclease activity for the point mutants) is covered by 'shared upon request to the corresponding author' - an on-request clause, which is an explicit A1 fail condition.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no table anywhere in the deposited data or the supplement file listing, so there is no label column. Any prediction target (e.g. 'does this Rad1 point mutation disrupt Saw1 binding?') would have to be constructed by reading values off figure panels in an 11.8 MB PDF - the textbook A2 failure.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs would be fine if a label existed: full protein sequences for Rad1 (1,100 residues), Rad10 (210) and Saw1 (261) are in the mmCIF files I opened, plus UniProt accessions P06777, P06838, P39735 text-mined from the paper.

a4_units_stated.note: No units because no measurement table exists. Assay readouts (percent survival, relative growth on spot assays) appear only as plotted figures.

a5_enough_rows.note: Verified in the files: the entire released dataset is 2 structures. The paper's mutational analysis covers on the order of a dozen to a few dozen engineered point mutants, far under the ~400-row floor for even a classification task.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small; size was never the problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: What is deposited matches what the paper says: two maps (EMD-75395, EMD-75396) and two coordinate sets at 4.5 and 3.7 Angstrom, exactly as stated.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not applicable in the good sense - there is no label to trace. The modelled coordinates are themselves a human-plus-software interpretation of a density map, so using them as a prediction target would mean predicting a modelling output, not a direct measurement.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the released data is two protein structures with no measured outcome attached, so nothing can be trained or honestly evaluated.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein sequence and structure around a contact surface to predict whether a point mutation breaks a repair-protein partnership.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example would be one engineered amino-acid substitution in the yeast DNA-repair protein Rad1, described by its sequence neighbourhood and its position in the 3.7 Angstrom structure I opened. Verified count of usable examples: 2 structures and a few dozen mutants described only in figures - far too few.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the mutation abolishes binding to a specific partner protein (Saw1 versus Rad14) and whether it disables one repair pathway but not the other. The true answer comes from yeast growth-survival assays and protein pull-down experiments, both of which exist only as figure panels in this paper.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups studying structure-specific nucleases would like a way to guess which surface residues are pathway-specific before doing the mutagenesis, but this paper supplies nowhere near enough measurements to learn that, and the measurements it has are not released.

ml_idea: None viable from this paper. The only release is two cryo-EM coordinate sets (PDB 10QY, 10QX) of the yeast Rad1-Rad10 nuclease with and without its targeting factor Saw1. Those are useful as input features to someone else's project (for example as a structural template for protein-protein interface prediction, or as a hard test case for AlphaFold-style complex prediction, since the paper reports that Rad1-Rad10 does not auto-inhibit the way human XPF-ERCC1 does), but they are not a dataset with a label and cannot be the basis of a training project.

effort.compute_note: Only the two mmCIF files were downloaded and parsed; total 1.8 MB, parsed in under a second. No modelling estimate is meaningful because no trainable dataset exists.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement and list the supplementary files - 2 minutes. It shows two structures plus 'all other data available on request' and zero tabular files, which kills the project before any download.

verdict_reason: This is a single-complex structural biology paper, not a dataset paper. The entire public release is two cryo-EM structures (verified: 10QY with 3 chains and 8,561 atoms at 3.7 Angstrom, 10QX with 2 chains and 6,512 atoms at 4.5 Angstrom) and a supplement that contains only figure images and one PDF. Part A fails four ways: A1, because every quantitative experimental result is 'shared upon request to the corresponding author'; A2, because there is no label column anywhere and any target would have to be read off figure panels; A5, because n = 2 structures and a few dozen unreleased mutant measurements; and A4, because no units exist where no measurement table exists. The structures are a genuine contribution to DNA-repair biology and are worth keeping as a test case for protein-complex prediction, but there is no machine-learning project here.
